result:
Every Thursday, someone left a flower on the bus.

Not a bouquet. One flower, tucked into the wire frame behind the driver’s seat: a daisy with a bent stem, a marigold still dusty from the garden, once a rose that smelled faintly of rain. By the last stop, it was always gone.

The driver never saw who brought them. He drove the early route, when everyone kept their eyes on their phones or the pale square of sky between buildings. He did see who took them. A nurse going home after a night shift. A boy who held a sunflower as carefully as a full cup. An old man who smiled at a small purple bloom, then put it back for someone else.

One Thursday, the frame was empty. The driver found himself looking at it all morning.

At lunch, he bought a bunch of carnations from the shop beside the depot. He put one behind his seat and left the rest on the dashboard, where anyone could reach them.
